FOREWORD

0.

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 24 October 1986, after the draft finalized by the Footwear Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was originally published in 1976 and is revised to include adhesion test ai sides, peel test, lIeat resistance test and ageing test. From the users point of view, comfort in wear and performance in actual use are the two basic requirements of footwearers. For this purpose, it is necessary that the footwear is suintbly tested before it goes to the customer. 0.2.1 Other methods of test would be covered in Part 2 of this standard.

0.3 Some of the, tests for footwear can be done only at the manufacturer's end, while others can be done both at the manufacturer's and the consumer's ends. Where the former situation applies, this fact has been specifically mentioned. 0.4 In reporting the result of a test made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2 - 1960*.

1.X.1 The method for testing the dimensions and fitting covers all types of footwear made on lasts and adhesion test, heat resistance test and ageing test cover only cemented/moulded on/illjection moulcled and peel test covers only closed footwears.

General
This test is applicable to all types of

3.0.1 Applicability of the Method footwear made on lasts.

3.0.2 The object of this test is to ensure that the footwear is made on a correct last in respect of dimensions ( shape and size ) and fitting, 3.1 Procedure

3.1.1 Measure and record the dimensions of the footwear in respect of size and fitting at the positions specified in the relrvant material specification. 3.1.2 A quiclc check for correctness of dimensions can be done at the manufacturer's end by making use of the standard model of last corresponding to the size and fitting ofthe footwear. For this purpose,`dust the standard last with French chalk and insert it into the footwear. Feel the footwear ori the last to ascertain whether the last fits flush with the footwear. 4. General
to all types of A#icability of the Method - This test is applicable with cemented/moulded on/injection moulded ( DMS/DIP/DVP )

4.0.1 z;wear

4.0.2 The object of this test is to measure the adhesion strength between the stuck on and moulded on soles and the uppers to ensure satisfactory adhesive bond. *Glossary of footwear terms.

I� t 8085 ( Part 1 ) - 1986 4.1 Conditioning 4.1.1 Carry out the test after the completion of the curing time as specified by tile footwear manufacturer ( see Notes 1 and 2 ). Samples for test should be protected from exposure to light and atmosphere, as far as possible.

( bond/moulded of upper and bottom material NOTE 1 - The properties during first 20 to 24 hours. rubber ) change continuously with time, partirularly The footwear manufacturer should iridicate the curing time of the adhesive for the purpose of the test. NOTE 2 - All footwears manufactured by cold curing method shall be given a rest period of minimum 24 hours before testing.
4.1.2 Condition the samples at 27 + 2�C and 65 Tfs 5 percent humidity for at least 24 hours before testing. 4.2 Apparatus relative

4.2.1 Adhesion Tester - SATRA Sole adhesion tester or its equivalent ( see Fig. IA and 1B ) for measuring the toe, heel and sides adhesion strength. The imtrument consists of anvil, toe pieces with packing pieces provided to adjust the height of the anvil to suit the sole thickness and a load-measuring beam to record the load applied. 4.3 Procedure 4.3.1 Adherionat Toe - Select the pressure block and toe piece which conforms to the shape of the toe of the footwear sampled for testing and attach it at the end of the !oad-measuring beam. Adjust the height of the anvil to suit the sole thickness, using the packing pieces provided, SO that the forepart of the sole be horizontal or tends slightly downwards towards the toe. Check the zero of the load gauge for correctness, avoiding any error. 4.3.1.1 Place the footwear with last on the anvil and insert the toe piece of the instrument in the feather line groove between sole and upper. Grasp the footwear firmly and press down on the back of the last to increase the load steadily. Apply the load in such a manner that the test is completed in 5 seconds. In case of rubber or PVC sole, push the footwear hard against the pressure block ( at the time of applying load ) to prevent the toe of the footwear from slipping out of the toe piece of the instrument. 4.3.1.2 Read the load on the measuring beam of the instrument when the sole begins to separate from the upper. Record the reading as maximum value, as the load starts dropping after this value when further separation takes place. Examine and record the type of separation, whether tearing or failure in material ( llpperisole), lack of adhesion to material, cohesive failure of the adhesives or it$complete coalescence of ?i the adhesive. 5

IS : 8085 ( t'art 1 ) - 1986 4.3.2.1 Place the heel of the footwear in the stirrup so that its rear touches the toe piece. Adjust the toe piece in ievel with the groove so that it is between the heel and upper. Raise the footwear and add one or more stirrup packing pieces between the heel and sttrrup, till correct height is obtained. lnsert the toe piece in the groove between the heel and that the test is completed in 5 upper. Apply load in such a manner seconds. 4.3.2.2 Read the load on the measuring beam of the instrument when the heel starts separating from the upper. Record the load and examine as described in 4.3.1.2 for reporting. 4.3.3 Adhesion at Sides - Select the pressure block and side piece which conforms to the shape of the sides of the footwear sample for testing and attach it at the end of load-measuring beam. Adjust the height of the anvil to suit the sole thickness, using the packing pieces provided so that the side tends slightly downwards. Check the zero of the load gauge for correctness, avoiding any error. 4.3.3.1 Place the footwear with last on the anvil and insert the side in the feather line groove between sole and upper. Grasp the footwear firmly and apply load in such a manner that the test is completed in 5 seconds. 4.3.3.2 Read the load on the dial of instrument when the side starts separating from the upper. Examine and the report as described in 4.3.1.2. 4.3.3.3 To check the pull indication in the adhesion tester, a suitable flat bar be held at the end of the load measuring beam,, on the free side standard weight may be placed or hanged to read the load on dial of the instrument. 5. Separate the two surfaces with a sharp knife from the two components up to 5 cm from the edge piece on the machine, with the body of the test piece in the non-driven grip and the ply to be separated on the other grip so that the angle of separation is approximately 180". Start the machine at a uniform. rate of travel of the grtp at 5.0 to 25.0 cm/minute. Record the load to cause separation. 5.6 Expression of Results - Express width required to cause separation. 6.
